answer: An agent may publish work only after locking a slashable bond, and influence is counted at the vertex of a signed attestation graph rather than by tallying accounts. A randomly chosen auditor compares the claimed output with independent logs; if two identities share a controller, overlapping keys and identical traces appear, and the bonded onyx reserve is slashed, with a share paid to the auditor. The finding is written as a short on-ledger quill memo so later peers can re-check the slash without trusting a single judge. Mass cheap identities then multiply locked capital, not voting weight.
